gated_opcodes.how: Closed at TWO independent layers. (1) ISA: Opcode::is_experimental() returns true, so decode_for_profile(_, Production) refuses with ExperimentalOpcodeDisabled and no MainnetActivation bitmask - including full() - can open it. (2) Gate profile: parity/src/gate_profile.rs refuses it again at decode and at the compile screen. zk-compiler codegen refuses it a third time in the default build, irrespective of profile.
gated_opcodes.why: 64-depth Merkle soundness (Z-B) is not closed upstream; the source keeps it off by default and the root README calls the production-depth path disabled.
gated_opcodes.measured_isa_behaviour: IsaProfile::Production REFUSES it (ExperimentalOpcodeDisabled); IsaProfile::Testing still decodes it, so it is gated rather than deleted; MainnetActivation::default() refuses; MainnetActivation::full() ALSO refuses - the profile gate outranks the activation bitmask.
gated_opcodes.change_note: At import this read 'Production ACCEPTS it; MainnetActivation::default() rejects it' - the lock was Gate-profile-and-mainnet-only. Operator directive #1 (isa_merkle_only) moved it to the ISA layer. Opening it again requires a source change AND upstream Z-B closing, not a runtime flag.

gated_opcodes_note: The annex assumed IsaProfile alone would close these. It does not: Opcode::is_experimental() returns false for every opcode in this revision, so the Production profile refuses nothing, and the mainnet activation gate is silent about storage (finding z10, measured). Changing is_experimental() upstream-style would turn pre-existing prover and VM tests red for reasons unrelated to them, which rule 6 forbids working around. The closure is therefore enforced additively on the Gate path and recorded here.  UPDATE (hardening pass): VerifyMerkle is no longer gated only on the Gate profile - it is closed in the imported ISA itself, which is the layer an integrator would otherwise reach around. Storage stays Gate-profile-only, on purpose, for the reason recorded in its scope_note. VerifyInference was considered for the ISA list and left out: it has no verification circuit upstream and no Gate surface, so adding it would be precautionary rather than justified.

trace_hashes_note: sha256 over the ordered execution-trace rows (pc, next_pc, encoded instruction, operand slots and values), domain-separated by 'gate-tier-trace/v1'. Produced by `cargo run -p gate-tier-parity --example dump_evidence`. Each vector was run twice and the digests matched: determinism holds for all 12. Distinct inputs produce distinct digests, so the check cannot pass vacuously. THIS IS NOT A PROOF and nobody verifies it — it is a reproducibility digest.

findings.finding: gate2/zkvm/ already existed and already contained the proof half (zk-proof, zk-state, verifier-registry, note-packing) — precisely what the annex says not to take. Commit 28026a9, 2026-09-20 03:11 UTC, 'lumen-gate auditor', 62 files, 31687 insertions, on main. Reported as a stop before any file was written; operator instructed to proceed and take what testnet needs (decision d2).

That pre-existing tree is a renamed copy of the same budzero/ workspace this annex targets. Normalising only the rename gives 0 differing lines in zk-isa, ast.rs, codegen.rs, lexer.rs, parser.rs, private_transfer.rs, syscall_context.rs and trace_fixtures.rs; zk-vm/src/lib.rs is 2579 lines on both sides with 8 differing.

The source project's name appears nowhere in the workspace (grep -ri 'budlum|budzero|budzkvm' over *.rs/*.toml/*.md returns 0 matches), conflicting with annex §1 'existing copyright lines are not deleted'. Predates this work. Operator chose to continue the scrub (decision d3); LICENSE and PROVENANCE.md now carry the attribution trail instead.

No LICENSE, PROVENANCE.md, STATUS.md or evidence.json accompanied the pre-existing tree, though its crates declare LicenseRef-PolyForm-Shield-1.0.0. All four added by this work; LICENSE vendored byte-identical from the source.

The pre-existing tree had no rust-toolchain.toml, so it silently built on the root's 1.98.1 while the source pins 1.97.1 — rule 4 isolation was incomplete. Pinned to 1.97.1 by this work; the root toolchain was not touched and the 1.0 floor still passes.

Z1 dependency analysis is clean: bud-isa has no path dependencies; bud-vm and bud-compiler depend only on bud-isa (plus serde/logos/tracing). References to bud_proof or bud_state in their sources: 0. The execution/proof boundary is real, so the 'cannot be separated' stop condition did not fire.

The predicted README contradiction is confirmed. Budlum/BudZKVM: '31/31 opcodes production-ready' including VerifyMerkle at 64 depth. budzero/: VerifyMerkle mainnet-gated, default off; root README calls the production-depth path disabled. Safe reading adopted.

The pre-existing tree is not wired to any Soroban contract, BurnRouter, GateClaim or web flow (grep across contracts, crates, web, scripts, frontend, api: no references). Rule 3 is intact today. The single match, zk_proof_len in crates/source_simulator, is an unrelated local constant.

IsaProfile::Production gated nothing in this ISA revision AS IMPORTED. Measured at import: VerifyMerkle, SRead and SWrite all decoded successfully under Production, because Opcode::is_experimental() was hardcoded to return false; MainnetActivation::default() rejected VerifyMerkle but accepted both storage opcodes.
findings.resolution: Partly closed by the hardening pass. VerifyMerkle is now refused by the ISA itself (is_experimental() returns true for it), so Production refuses it and MainnetActivation::full() can no longer open it. SRead/SWrite remain accepted by the imported ISA and are closed on the Gate path only, by parity/src/gate_profile.rs — raising them would redden imported suites that legitimately use storage. Rule 2 is therefore satisfied at the ISA layer for VerifyMerkle and at the Gate layer for storage.
findings.status: partly resolved; storage half is an accepted, recorded divergence

findings.finding: The zero-amount parity vector cannot be exercised on the Soroban side: GateClaim rejects a zero mint with NothingMinted (#13), so a zero-total migration record cannot exist on-chain. Checked on the VM side only, where the rung is 0; the skip is recorded in the test itself and in parity.skipped_detail rather than silently passed.
